title: Merchant-Facing Decision Card Schema v1
description: Schema for the merchant-facing decision card: the output artifact that tells a merchant what pattern was detected, why, what to do about it, and what the expected outcome is. This is distinct from the customer-facing copy output. It follows the diagnostic flow: Pattern Detected → Evidence Chain → Diagnosis → Likely Causes → Checks → Recommendation → Expected Impact.

card_id.description: Unique identifier for this decision card instance.

rule_id.description: The playbook rule that fired and produced this card.

run_id.description: The pipeline run that produced this card. Links to the run_receipt.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this card was generated.

merchant_id.description: Identifier for the merchant this card is addressed to. Optional for batch runs.

pattern_detected.description: A single sentence naming the pattern that fired (e.g. 'Replenishment overdue for high-value customers'). This is the headline the merchant reads first.

diagnosis_summary.description: Two-to-three sentence diagnostic explanation: what the data shows, what it implies, and what the likely root cause is. Corresponds to the 'because' field in the playbook.

evidence_chain.description: The ordered chain of observations and implications that support the diagnosis. Mirrors the playbook's diagnostic_logic.evidence_chain, populated with run-specific values where available.

observation.description: What the data shows at this step (may include run-specific values).

observed_value.description: The actual run-time value observed (optional; numeric or string).

checks_to_run.description: Verification checks the merchant (or the system) should confirm before acting. For HYPOTHESIS cards these are the primary output; for RECOMMENDATION cards they represent pre-action validation steps.

confirm_if.description: The condition that confirms this check passes.

status.description: Runtime status of this check (filled in during or after execution).

recommendations.description: Priority-ordered list of recommended actions for the merchant. Priority 1 is the highest-urgency, highest-confidence action.

recommendation.description: Specific, actionable recommendation text. Must be specific (what exactly to do), diagnostic (why this action), and tied to the observed pattern.

automation_level.description: How much human review is required before this action executes.

preconditions.description: Named conditions that must be met before this action is valid.

why.description: Plain-language explanation of why these recommendations are the right response to this pattern. This is the 'compelling' component: what makes it worth acting on now.

why_not.description: Explicit list of actions the merchant should NOT take, with reasons. Prevents common over-reactions or misdiagnoses.

reason.description: Why taking this action would be wrong or counterproductive in this context.

risk_notes.description: Caveats, assumptions, or risk flags the merchant should be aware of before acting.

confidence.description: Overall confidence in the diagnosis and recommendations, given the available evidence at run time.

expected_impact_proxy.description: The expected business outcome if the merchant follows the recommendations. Expressed as a proxy when exact ROI is unavailable.

description.description: One-to-two sentence impact statement tied to observable business metrics.

key_metrics.description: The metrics expected to improve (e.g. CAC, repurchase_rate, contribution_margin).

estimated_improvement.description: Directional magnitude estimate (e.g. '-15% CAC over 30 days', '+20pp repurchase rate within one cycle').

validation_status.description: RECOMMENDATION: sufficient evidence to act confidently. HYPOTHESIS: surface checks and likely causes only, do not act yet. INSUFFICIENT_DATA: required data sources missing; escalate or defer.
